notes: GenApp's VSAM 'delete policy' (LGDPVS01, LINKed by LGDPDB01): WF-POLICY-KEY = CA-REQUEST-ID(4:1) + CA-CUSTOMER-NUM + CA-POLICY-NUM, then EXEC CICS DELETE FILE('KSDSPOLY') RIDFLD(WF-Policy-Key) KEYLENGTH(21); on NORMAL it GOBACKs. Each scenario's KSDSPOLY is compared after the task. Every non-NORMAL RESP in this program goes to WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE, whose first act is EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('LGSTSQ') (GenApp's TS/TD error logger). The harness runs one program, but the case's programs list adds LGSTSQ to the same task (X6, #4607), so the error paths run: NOTFND for a key not on file and IOERR on the DELETE (CA-RETURN-CODE '81'). A task that reaches WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE is judged only up to LGSTSQ's FIRST LINK (the 102-byte ERROR-MSG: this program's message is 17 bytes longer than LGACVS01's 85), where LGSTSQ writes 107 bytes (EIBCALEN + 5) from a 95-byte WRITE-MSG and the oracle refuses that WRITEQ TD by name (X6, LENGTH past FROM; IBM leaves it undefined); the RESP and the file are compared before it, the end state is not. So the proof never reaches WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE's COMMAREA copy (lines 117-131): its 4 branch outcomes stay uncovered until X6 is modelled (#5252). The faults list injects the file RESPs a healthy data set cannot give (IOERR, NOSPACE); the region ASSIGN SYSID is a deployment fact the corpus does not name. NOTOPEN / DISABLED are not injected. Keys: WF-POLICY-KEY is the request-type byte followed by 20 digits, so every key mixes a letter and digits; No browse is issued, so no key order is exercised (the comparison sorts each side's records by key bytes). Data: ksdspoly.txt is built from GenApp's own sample policies (base/cntl/db2cre.jcl's policy rows joined with their endowment / house / motor / commercial rows), laid out as WF-POLICY-INFO (request-type letter + customer + policy number, then the type's 43 bytes) -- the record LGAPVS01 writes; policy 7 (type C, no commercial row) is left out.
